dish: Hakodate wine (since 1973) — free tastings of 12+ wines and the shop-only wine soft-serve
n: Hakodate Wine Budōkan Honten (はこだてわいん 葡萄館本店)
address: Kamifujishiro 11, Nanae, Kameda District, Hokkaido, Japan
w: One of Hokkaido's pioneer wineries (1973): about 80 wines on the shelves, a dozen to taste free, and a wine soft-serve sold only here.

dish: Mori ikameshi — squid stuffed with rice, the town's original ekiben
n: Michi-no-eki YOU・Yū・Mori (道の駅 YOU・遊・もり)
address: Kamidai-chō 326-18, Mori, Kayabe District, Hokkaido, Japan
w: Route 5 roadside station of Mori, home of ikameshi — the squid-rice ekiben sold here in many forms, with Komagatake and Uchiura Bay from the roof lounge.

dish: Matsumae hon-maguro-don (Tsugaru Strait bluefin) and Matsumae-zuke
n: Michi-no-eki Kitamaebune Matsumae (道の駅 北前船 松前)
w: Clifftop roadside station on the Tsugaru Strait serving bowls of wild bluefin from the same waters as Ōma tuna, and Matsumae-zuke, the clan-era pickle of herring roe, kelp and squid.

dish: tekkui-don — tempura of local wild flounder ('tekkui') over rice
n: Michi-no-eki Kaminokuni Monju (道の駅 上ノ国もんじゅ)
w: Sea-of-Japan roadside station whose restaurant window looks over the water; the signature is a tendon of local flounder.

dish: junmai sake brewed with Daisetsu snowmelt water (sold mainly in Kamikawa)
n: Kamikawa Taisetsu Shuzō Ryokkyū-gura (上川大雪酒造 緑丘蔵)
address: Asahi-machi, Kamikawa, Kamikawa District, Hokkaido, Japan
w: A 2017 regional-revival sake brewery at the foot of Daisetsuzan — pure sake only, from Hokkaido rice and mountain water.

dish: Asahikawa shinkoyaki — a charcoal-grilled half young chicken in a sauce kept going since 1925
n: Yakitori Senmon Ginneko (焼鳥専門 ぎんねこ)
w: The keeper of Asahikawa's soul food: a 1925 yakitori house in the Fura-Ri-To alley grilling a whole half chicken over charcoal in its never-emptied tare.

dish: Taisetsu ji-beer (4–5 on tap, Daisetsu water) with lamb jingisukan
w: A red-brick warehouse brewpub five minutes from Asahikawa Station pouring the local Taisetsu beers alongside fresh-lamb jingisukan.

dish: Furano wine — factory-only seasonal bottlings and free tastings
n: Furano Wine Factory (ふらのワイン工場)
address: Shimizuyama, Furano Budōgaoka Park, Furano, Hokkaido, Japan
w: The city-run brick winery on Shimizuyama hill (grapes since 1972): see the cellar and bottle-ageing rooms and taste factory-exclusive wines, free entry.

dish: Furano produce, cheese, milk and wine — JA Furano farm store and takeout stalls
w: Four buildings round a plaza near Furano Station: JA Furano's farm shop, a sweets bakery, ~2,000 local products and takeout stands cooking local ingredients.

dish: award-winning Niseko-milk cheeses (blue 'Kū', aged mimolette-style 'Momiji') and camembert soft-serve
n: Niseko Cheese Kōbō (ニセコチーズ工房)
address: Kondō 425-6, Niseko, Abuta District, Hokkaido, Japan
w: Small creamery making cheese from Niseko milk — World Cheese Awards 2021 super-gold for its long-aged 'Momiji' — with a café selling camembert soft-serve in summer.

dish: hand-cut kiko-uchi (100% buckwheat) soba and kamo-seiro; soba kaiseki by reservation
address: Niseko 431, Niseko, Abuta District, Hokkaido, Japan
w: Soba master Tatsuru Rai's tiny counter (opened 2000) — the Niseko soba made famous by Anthony Bourdain's No Reservations; dinner is reservation-only.

dish: French-Japanese tasting menu of Niseko produce (chef Yuichi Kamimura, ex-Tetsuya's)
address: Hirafu, Kutchan, Abuta District, Hokkaido, Japan
w: Niseko's fine-dining pioneer (2008): chef Yuichi Kamimura, trained under Tetsuya Wakuda in Sydney, holds a Michelin star from the Hokkaido guide.

dish: ohoro GIN (13 botanicals incl. Niseko mint) — ISC 2024 gin Trophy — and single malt
address: Niseko 478-15, Niseko, Abuta District, Hokkaido, Japan
w: Opened 2021 beside Niseko's onsen area with Scottish pot stills and Annupuri spring water; its ohoro gin took the top gin award at the 2024 International Spirits Challenge.

dish: genshu sake from Yōtei spring water — about 30 to taste (since 1916)
address: Asahi 47, Kutchan, Abuta District, Hokkaido, Japan
w: Kutchan's century-old (1916) sake brewery at the foot of Yōtei, known for undiluted genshu; around 30 sakes to taste and buy, 15 minutes' walk from Kutchan Station.
